children: Goeasy shares were sharply lower Wednesday after it swung to a loss in the third quarter, driven by a drop in revenue and a sharp rise in bad debt expenses tied to its troubled auto and powersports portfolios.
Shares traded 18% lower at 36.99 Canadian dollars ($26.07), and are now down about 72% year-to-date.
The embattled nonprime lender reported late Tuesday that it swung to a loss of C$17 million, or C$1.03 a share, from a profit of C$28.4 million, or C$1.70 a share. in the prior-year period.

Goeasy has been facing a protracted operational crisis after errors in delinquency reporting and payment-in-transit accounting across its LendCare auto and powersports portfolio triggered restatements, surging charge-offs, and debt-covenant amendments earlier this year.
On an adjusted basis, the loss was of C$0.94 a share, wider than the C$0.37 per-share loss expected by analysts, according to FactSet.

Revenue fell to C$371.6 million from C$454.2 million, coming in slightly better than the C$368.5 million analysts expected. The company noted that gross consumer loans receivable was down 10% at C$4.88 billion from the prior year, and down 2% sequentially, and was one of the main reasons for the revenue decline.

In the third quarter, goeasy's net charge-off rate, a key credit metric that measures confirmed loan losses, climbed to 15.2%, up 620 basis points from the prior-year quarter, although it improved 150 basis points sequentially from 16.7% in the second quarter.
Bad debts rose to C$214.9 million from C$177.5 million.

The company noted that the total allowance for credit losses on gross consumer loans at quarter's end increased to C$516.3 million from C$451.7 million last year mainly due to the company's revised assessment of collectability and an increase in the credit-loss outlook for merchant-originated automotive and powersports loans.
